title: He didn’t pick one stone.
paragraphs: He didn’t pick one stone.
He picked five.
Before David ever stepped onto the battlefield, before the sling was swung, before the giant fell… there was a quiet moment by a small stream.

The armies of Israel and the Philistines were facing each other across the Valley of Elah.
For forty days, Goliath had stepped forward, shouting his challenge.

Mocking.
Defying.
Intimidating.
And every soldier in Israel stepped back in fear.
Except one shepherd boy.
But before David confronted the giant, Scripture tells us something small that most people overlook.
“Then he took his staff in his hand and chose five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in a shepherd’s pouch.” — 1 Samuel 17:40
Five stones.
Not one.
Why?
Some people assume David picked five stones because he lacked confidence.
But if you read the story carefully, the opposite is true.
David was the only person in the entire army who was absolutely convinced of victory.
He told King Saul:
“The Lord who rescued me from the paw of the lion and the paw of the bear will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine.” (1 Samuel 17:37)
David did not step into that valley hoping God might help.
He stepped into that valley knowing God would help.
So why five stones?
Because faith does not cancel wisdom.
David trusted God completely.
But he still prepared.

Faith is not reckless.
Faith is responsible.
Throughout Scripture, God works through people who trust Him and prepare.
Noah trusted God — but he still built the ark.
Joseph trusted God — but he still stored grain during the years of abundance.
Nehemiah trusted God — but the builders held swords while rebuilding the wall.
Faith moves forward with preparation.
And David understood something powerful:
Victory belongs to God, but preparation belongs to us.
There’s another fascinating detail many readers miss.
Later in Scripture, we learn that Goliath was not the only giant connected to his family.
In fact, several giants from Gath appear later in Israel’s battles (2 Samuel 21:15–22).
Some scholars suggest David may have taken five stones because he was prepared in case other giants stepped forward.
Whether that was the reason or not, the lesson remains powerful.
David wasn’t careless.
He was ready.
He had a sling in his hand.
Five stones in his pouch.
And absolute confidence in his God.
The truth is, many people want the miracle without the preparation.
We pray for open doors but never develop the skills.
We ask God for influence but never build character.
We hope for victory but avoid discipline.
But David shows us a different path.

Trust God fully.
Prepare faithfully.
Step forward courageously.
And when the moment comes, God can use even the smallest things.
A shepherd boy.
A sling.
One stone.
That stone flew through the air, struck the giant’s forehead, and in a single moment the battle shifted.
The giant that terrified an army fell before a boy who trusted God.
And the entire valley witnessed a truth that still echoes through history:
The size of the giant never determines the outcome of the battle.
God does.
But notice something important.
David had five stones…
Yet he only needed one.
Because when preparation meets faith, and faith meets obedience, God moves in ways that change everything.
Maybe the giants in your life look intimidating right now.

Fear.
Pressure.
Uncertainty.
Challenges that seem bigger than you.
But the story of David reminds us of something powerful.
Giants don’t fall because of our strength.
Giants fall because God fights for those who trust Him.
But don’t miss the quiet lesson beside the stream.
David believed God would win the battle.
Yet he still filled his pouch.
Because true faith isn’t passive.
True faith prepares.

And sometimes the difference between fear and courage…
between defeat and victory…
between standing back and stepping forward…
…is simply picking up the stones God placed within your reach.
One step.
One act of faith.
One prepared heart.
And suddenly the giant that once looked unstoppable begins to fall.
So remember this the next time you face something that feels impossible:
Faith trusts God.
Wisdom prepares.
And when those two walk together, giants don’t stand a chance.
What do you think?
Did David pick five stones as backup…
or was he preparing in case more giants stepped forward?
